name: Awa Bancha
categoryNote: A lactic-fermented Japanese tea filed with the dark class by process. Not 渥堆, not English black tea, not a failed sencha.

harvest.note: Bancha as in late leaf — the calendar is the name. This is not first-flush sencha.

pluckStandard: mature summer leaf, boiled then lactic-fermented

transformation.note: Anaerobic lactic fermentation after a boil, then sun-dry. Microbial, not enzymatic oxidation, and not puer-style 渥堆.

processing.description: Summer mature leaf in Tokushima. The 晩 is the point.
Leaf is boiled, not steamed as sencha and not wok-fired as a Chinese green.
Packed anaerobic until lactic acid bacteria sour the leaf. Related in spirit to goishicha; not a wet pile in the Yunnan sense.
Unpacked and dried. The sour-pickle register is the process, not a fault.

infusions.notes: longer first steep; this leaf does not open like sencha

gongfu.curveException: Awa bancha is not a Japanese needle green. The first steep is long because the leaf is boiled-and-dried, not rolled-open.

decoction.when: a kettle on the table, as the villages often drink it
decoction.notes: 煮茶 — simmering is ordinary here. The sour is already in the leaf; heat just lifts it.

water.note: Near boiling is fine. Soft water keeps the sour clean rather than metallic.

storage: Airtight. The pickle aroma will scent nearby sencha. Stable compared with ichibancha.

shelfLife.window: a year or more in a tin
shelfLife.note: Most teas are food. A few teas are projects.

qualityMarkers.claim: clean lactic sour, not dirty compost

commonFaults.name: confused with hojicha because both are “brown”

compare.differentiator: Everyday bancha is steamed green. Awa bancha is boiled and lactic-fermented — a different class, same late-leaf calendar.

summary: Tokushima’s lactic late tea: boiled, pickled, sun-dried. A dark tea that tastes of sour plum, not of 渥堆.
